subject.title: perf: avoid event-loop stall during embedded_run bootstrap-context

question: Should OpenClaw accept the custom yielding glob walker and bootstrap-hook scheduling as the bounded fix for this event-loop stall despite possible prompt-order and session-interleaving changes?
rationale: The patch has no concrete correctness finding and direct-path proof is strong, but bootstrap glob semantics and hook timing are shipped context and session behavior that automation should not redefine without owner intent.

options.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
options.body: Accept the bounded compatibility risk, refresh onto current main, and merge after exact-head focused and changed-lane validation.

options.title: Require Live Channel Proof
options.body: Keep the implementation shape but request one current-head embedded-run with active channel I/O showing the original stall no longer suppresses timers or message delivery.

options.title: Pause For Broader Architecture
options.body: Do not land this branch if owners prefer worker isolation, priority scheduling, or another runtime design instead of maintaining a custom glob walker.

recommendation.title: Land After Exact-Head Verification
recommendation.body: Accept the bounded compatibility risk, refresh onto current main, and merge after exact-head focused and changed-lane validation.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest merged history spans the internal hook, bootstrap hook, and guarded workspace-read boundaries affected by the decision.
